title: Gaussian-process optimization raises measured surfactin titer in laboratory fermentation
summary: Using 25 batch experiments with Bacillus subtilis MTCC 2423, Gaussian-process regression predicted surfactin titers and selected fermentation conditions. The optimized condition produced 5.75 ± 0.09 g/L, compared with a 1.49 g/L base case. The result is specific to this strain and laboratory process.
organization: Birla Institute of Technology and Science Pilani, K.K. Birla Goa Campus

evidence.tested: A GPR-selected fermentation condition was experimentally checked and yielded 5.75 ± 0.09 g/L surfactin versus a 1.49 g/L base case, following 25 batch experiments.
evidence.unknown: The measured result is for B. subtilis MTCC 2423 under the reported laboratory conditions; industrial performance is not established.
evidence.ai_role: GPR models titer from fermentation conditions and constrains a search for an optimum that is then tested experimentally.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
